name: Hangtown Motocross Classic track (Prairie City SVRA)
address: 13300 White Rock Road, Rancho Cordova, CA 95742
tracks_on_site: national MX track inside Prairie City State Vehicular Recreation Area

soil.notes: Naturally hard-packed - once called the hardest dirt on the schedule. Sand and rice hulls have been added for about 20 years, and more sand went in for 2024, giving more depth and grip. The hillside stays rock hard and edgy.

traits: big braking bumps at downhill bottoms
layout.notes: Long downhills where most passes happen by out-braking at the bottom; two lines usually form over large braking bumps. Layout was opened up in 2024 with fewer tight switchbacks; a downhill double section had its lips removed after crashes.

conditions.dry: Hot (often near 100F) and dries quickly; surface water just puddles on hard dirt and makes it slicker.
conditions.late_day: Dries and firms up by second motos and deteriorates through the day.
conditions.watering_prep: Testers say it only works when soaked and ripped in deep ahead of time; late surface watering fails.
conditions.seasonal: Pro national held each late May/early June by the Dirt Diggers North club (since 1969; at Prairie City since 1979).

rider_reports.says: Analyst: imported soils made it far better than the old hardpack, but it is still not RedBud-soft; the hillside is rock hard, and scoop tires trade hard-pack feel for start traction.
Analyst: sand added for 2024 gave more traction and depth; track dried and hardened by moto two and a big braking bump formed at a downhill double takeoff.
Analyst: 2023 prep missed; hot sun dried it, late watering puddled and reduced traction; hard base gives choppy, jarring bumps. Riders said more water should have gone down earlier.

name: Mammoth Motocross
address: Motocross Access Road, Mammoth Lakes, CA 93546

soil.notes: Directory lists loamy soil, decomposed granite and sand. A 2006 rider account says the loose winter topsoil gets roosted into the trees after a few practices, leaving a rocky track.

layout.notes: Natural mountain layout at about 7,700-8,000 ft. Thin air cuts engine power sharply.

conditions.dry: Smooth early, then very rough and rocky once topsoil is roosted off.
conditions.late_day: Much rougher by heat races than in morning practice.
conditions.seasonal: Open only for the late-June Mammoth Motocross race event; limited practice passes.

rider_reports.says: Rider column: practice starts smooth but loose topsoil is roosted away within a few sessions, leaving a rocky track; thin air makes a 125 feel badly down on power.
MXA columnist: at altitude tire pressure, fork air and shock nitrogen pressure rise; check and bleed before riding.

name: Pala Raceway (formerly Fox Raceway at Pala)
address: 12799 Hwy 76, Pala, CA 92059 (Pala Band of Mission Indians land)
tracks_on_site: national/pro outdoor track (practice layout differs from the race layout)
supercross track (opened late 2021; AMA pro license required)

soil.notes: Race coverage describes a very hard base under a sandy, slippery top layer that hardens if ridden aggressively or baked by sun. Riders call the dirt among the best in SoCal but warn of rocks on the hillsides. A directory says groomed loam; that is promo-level and not confirmed by racers.

layout.notes: Hillside national layout with long, fast sections that make passing hard. Pros note rocks that appear on the hills without warning.

conditions.dry: Loose top layer blows off or bakes hard in sun, leaving a slick hard base. Warmer September dates harden more than cool May dates.
conditions.wet: Watering the night before and morning of creates heavy ruts early; no true rain-race reports found.
conditions.late_day: Ruts harden by second motos and become hazardous (2024 report called the back section a land mine).
conditions.watering_prep: Track watered Friday night and Saturday morning before nationals.
conditions.seasonal: Public practice Mon-Tue 9am-2pm and Fri-Sun 9am-4pm per directory (Feb 2025). Hosts the Pro Motocross opener (late May). Renamed Pala Raceway presented by Fox Racing in Oct 2026.

rider_reports.says: Analyst: base is very hard; once loose dirt blows off, ruts in the back section set up hard and make second motos treacherous.
Preview: sandy yet slippery surface with deep sections; best riders stay light on the bike and short-shift to a taller gear to limit wheelspin.
Pros praise the dirt but flag big rocks on the hills, long fast sections and few passing spots; one calls it the best practice track in California.
A veteran pro called it a hard, blown-out California track that did not suit his style.
